outcome: Correct media seeking, selected-audio bounds, cache provenance and subprocess input isolation after the perception review.
criteria: Video frame extraction seeks near each requested timestamp while preserving the original presentation timestamp and frame content; decoding timeouts no longer suggest unavailable clipping tools.
Audio clipping uses the selected track endpoint on the video clock, including longer and delayed tracks, with an explicit container-duration fallback and accurate range diagnostics.
Audio cache identity includes the shared video reader code and timing facts, and FFmpeg, FFprobe and ASR subprocesses cannot consume MCP stdin.

Focused regressions and real FFmpeg container checks cover remote video frames, audio beyond the video endpoint, timestamp offsets, cache invalidation and stdin isolation; record validation and rebuild the usable media image.

dispositions.note: Absolute input seeking with automatic seek trimming disabled preserves full-decode PTS and PNG hashes for VFR, long GOPs and distinct clock origins. Timeouts report unread coverage.

Selected-track endpoints include audio offsets and can exceed video duration. Container fallback is explicit and estimated; extraction stops at actual EOF without trailing padding, and errors identify the audio track and range.
Requests hash video.py, audio.py and asr.py plus audio bounds and video origin. FFmpeg, FFprobe and ASR receive DEVNULL stdin; cache invalidation and isolation regressions pass.

Local suite: 263 passed, 6 real-media tests skipped. Rebuilt image passed all 19 media tests without source mounts. A 994.07-second 1080p30 synthetic clip yielded six late frames in 1.08 seconds, versus 16.85 seconds for full decoding of the final frame, with identical PTS and PNG hash.

note: All four review findings are addressed in the harness, with no backend or scenario-specific extraction changes. Generic synthetic fixtures cover long and delayed audio, selected-track bounds, VFR and nonzero timestamp origins, shared-reader cache identity, EOF coverage and stdin isolation. Documentation and host traces retain estimated bounds separately from the decoded interval.
